title: 3D Architectural Map of the HC-FMUSP Hospital Complex
summary: A three-dimensional isometric view of Hospital das Clínicas in São Paulo built from OpenStreetMap footprints and rendered in Blender Cycles. It highlights the CeAC employee care clinic in orange to anchor where healthcare-worker swabs were collected.
caption: Three-dimensional view of HC-FMUSP and neighbouring institutions in São Paulo. CeAC, where the healthcare-worker specimens were collected, is highlighted in orange. Building footprints, floor counts, streets, and green areas derive from OpenStreetMap (ODbL), with 3D rendering produced in Blender 5.3 (Cycles).
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 7.

title: Paired RT-qPCR and Metagenomic Concordance Matrix
summary: Side-by-side clinical concordance across Influenza A, Rhinovirus, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 workflow controls. Paired circle sizes compare RT-qPCR cycle-threshold intervals directly against metagenomic read counts for every sequenced specimen.
caption: Paired RT-qPCR and metagenomic observations for influenza A (FLUA), rhinovirus (RNV), and RSV arranged by sample identifier on the left, with SARS-CoV-2 workflow controls shown on the right. RT-qPCR circle sizes follow Ct intervals (larger symbols indicate lower Ct values and higher viral load), while metagenomic circle sizes represent sequence read-count intervals.
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 12.

title: São Paulo Forest-Cover Loss and Entomological Sampling Sites
summary: Multi-scale GIS map combining Global Forest Watch tree-cover layers with high-resolution QGIS insets of three Atlantic Forest edge sites (PEAL, PEC, and Terra Preta). A radial ring chart summarizes forest cover and tree-cover loss across São Paulo State.
caption: Entomological collection sites in PEAL, PEC, and Terra Preta (panels A, B, and C) in the Metropolitan Region of São Paulo. Detailed site insets were built in QGIS from OpenStreetMap vector layers. The ring graphic in the upper-left panel summarizes São Paulo State land cover (dense forest, secondary forest, 2000 to 2020 tree-cover loss, and urban or agricultural land) using Global Forest Watch layers.
sourceTitle: Vertebrate Hosts of Mosquito Blood Meals Following the YFV Outbreak
citation: Coelho-Rocha E, Fernandes LN, Valença IN, Mirza JD, Mucci LF, Pereira M, et al. Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State. Parasites & Vectors. 2026. Figure 1.

title: Targeted PCR vs. Metagenomic Detection and Read Abundance
summary: Three-panel diagnostic benchmark quantifying what nanopore metagenomics adds beyond a targeted respiratory panel. It links virus-specific detection proportions with a log-linear regression of viral read counts against RT-qPCR Ct values (R = -0.61, p = 0.0005).
caption: (A) Virus-specific proportions detected by PCR only, both methods, or metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) only, with total detections plotted as a grey line. (B) RT-qPCR Ct values plotted against log10 viral read counts with fitted regression line and confidence band. (C) Median metagenomic read abundance across Ct intervals.
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 11.

title: Wenzhou Sobemo-Like Virus 4: Phylogeny, Coverage, and Entropy
summary: Integrated genomic characterization of the first Wenzhou sobemo-like virus 4 genomes recovered from Aedes albopictus in Latin America. Combines a global map-linked maximum-likelihood tree, read-depth confidence intervals, sliding-window Shannon entropy, and ORF architecture.
caption: (A) Maximum-likelihood tree of complete genomes related to WSLV4 with world map circles scaled by genome count. (B) Mean sequencing depth across the three newly assembled WSLV4 genomes with 95% confidence intervals. (C) Nucleotide Shannon entropy along the genome. (D) Annotated open reading frames and relative gene positions.
sourceTitle: First Report of Wenzhou Sobemo-Like Virus 4 in Aedes albopictus
citation: Andrade PS, Valença IN, Heinisch MRS, Rocha EC, Fernandes LN, Faria NR, et al. First Report of Wenzhou sobemo-like virus 4 in Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae) in Latin America. Viruses. 2022;14(11):2341. Figure 2.

title: Seasonal Specimen Distribution and Viral Load Profiles
summary: Weekly epidemiological curve across the 2022 respiratory season in São Paulo paired with RT-qPCR Ct distributions across RSV, rhinovirus, influenza A, and SARS-CoV-2 controls (Kruskal-Wallis p = 4.9e-17), distinguishing sequenced and unsequenced swabs.
caption: (A) Weekly respiratory specimen counts during 2022 stratified by targeted panel result (RSV, rhinovirus, influenza A, and panel-negative specimens) alongside the Omicron surge window. (B) RT-qPCR Ct distributions across viral targets and SARS-CoV-2 workflow controls with boxplots (medians and interquartile ranges) and jittered observations colored by sequencing selection.
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 10.

title: Yellow Fever Virus Phylogeny and Spatial Outbreak Context
summary: Geographic and phylogenetic placement of a yellow fever virus genome recovered from a female Haemagogus leucocelaenus mosquito within the Brazilian South America 1 outbreak, mapping Brazilian states alongside host categories (mosquito, human, non-human primate).
caption: Maximum-likelihood phylogeny of the YFV South America 1 genotype integrating complete genomes from the 2017 to 2018 Brazilian outbreak and the genome recovered from Hg. leucocelaenus in this study. Tip colors indicate Brazilian states (RJ, SP, ES, MG, GO, TO) and right-hand bars encode host type. Rooted with an outgroup sequence from Aotus azarae infulatus (MF370545.1).
sourceTitle: Vertebrate Hosts of Mosquito Blood Meals Following the YFV Outbreak
citation: Coelho-Rocha E, Fernandes LN, Valença IN, Mirza JD, Mucci LF, Pereira M, et al. Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State. Parasites & Vectors. 2026. Figure 2.

title: Global Canine Distemper Virus Phylogeny and Temporal Signal
summary: Complete-genome maximum-likelihood phylogeny of global canine distemper virus (CDV) genotypes with a zoomed Europe/South America 1 subtree and a root-to-tip molecular clock regression (R² = 0.66, n = 52) confirming strong temporal signal across spillover lineages.
caption: (A) Global maximum-likelihood phylogeny inferred from publicly available complete CDV genomes (>15 kb) with major genotypes annotated and Brazilian marmoset (Callithrix penicillata) isolates highlighted in red. (B) Europe/South America 1 clade colored by country of origin. (C) Root-to-tip genetic divergence regression against sampling year showing clock-like evolution (R² = 0.66).
sourceTitle: Genomic Epidemiology of Canine Distemper Virus in Neotropical Primates
citation: Bertanhe M, Cabral MG, Valença IN, Nacif CL, Claro IM, Diniz LA, et al. Genomic Epidemiology of Canine Distemper Virus (CDV) in Neotropical Primates in Brazil Reveals Multiple Spillover Events and Convergent Evolution at Hemagglutinin Residue 519. bioRxiv. 2026. Figure 2.

title: Clinical Cohort Selection and Metagenomic Yield Schematic
summary: Visual study flow tracing 291 symptomatic healthcare workers from SARS-CoV-2 screening and respiratory-panel testing through nanopore metagenomic sequencing, linking each branch to the exact viruses detected.
caption: Study workflow and sample selection for nanopore metagenomic sequencing. Screening branches separate SARS-CoV-2 antigen-positive controls, respiratory-panel positive specimens (RSV, rhinovirus, influenza A), and 109 panel-negative specimens selected for agnostic metagenomics, with recovered viral taxa listed at right.
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 8.

title: Viral Taxonomic Assignments Across Sequenced Libraries
summary: Reads-per-million (RPM) bubble matrix comparing all viral taxa recovered from respiratory-panel positive versus panel-negative specimens, highlighting pathogens missed by targeted PCR such as human parainfluenza viruses, seasonal coronaviruses, and enteroviruses.
caption: Viral taxonomic assignments across sequenced clinical specimens and libraries. Columns list library-barcode identifiers grouped by Viral Panel Positive and Viral Panel Negative status; rows show assigned viral taxa; circle sizes encode reads-per-million (RPM) abundance tiers.
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 13.

title: End-to-End Bioinformatics Pipeline for Nanopore Metagenomics
summary: Structured computational architecture diagram tracing raw nanopore signal through Dorado basecalling, GRCh38 host depletion, dual read- and contig-level viral classification (Kraken 2, metaFlye, BLAST, DIAMOND, VirSorter), coverage profiling, and IQ-TREE 2 phylogenetics.
caption: Computational stages and analytical evidence used for interpretation in the doctoral thesis. Shaded modules group read preparation, candidate viral identification (taxonomic classification, de novo assembly, translated search, and exploratory VirSorter screening), reference coverage analysis, and maximum-likelihood phylogenetic reconstruction.
sourceTitle: PhD Thesis: Nanopore Metagenomics for Respiratory Virus Detection
citation: Valença IN. Nanopore metagenomics for respiratory virus detection and genomic characterization in São Paulo. PhD Thesis, University of São Paulo & Imperial College London, 2026. Figure 9.

title: Multiplex PCR vs. Rapid SMART-9N Benchmark on SARS-CoV-2
summary: Three-panel sequencing benchmark across clinical SARS-CoV-2 samples comparing tiling-amplicon multiplex PCR against agnostic Rapid SMART-9N metagenomics across genome coverage depth, Ct sensitivity curves, and read N50 length.
caption: Comparison of multiplex PCR and Rapid SMART-9N results for SARS-CoV-2 clinical samples (n = 10). (A) Mean genome coverage depth with 95% confidence ribbons across genome coordinates. (B) Proportion of mapped viral reads and percentage of genome covered at >=20x depth across RT-qPCR Ct values. (C) Per-sample read N50 comparison in base pairs.
sourceTitle: Rapid Viral Metagenomics Using SMART-9N and Nanopore Sequencing
citation: Claro IM, Ramundo MS, Coletti TM, da Silva CAM, Valença IN, Candido DS, et al. Rapid viral metagenomics using SMART-9N amplification and nanopore sequencing. Wellcome Open Research. 2021;6:241 (v2, 2023). Figure 4.

title: Urban Green-Area Coverage and Mosquito Sampling Parks in São Paulo
summary: Nested geographic context map moving from South America and Brazil to São Paulo State and a district-level green-area coverage choropleth of São Paulo city, pinpointing the two urban parks sampled for Aedes albopictus.
caption: Nested spatial maps showing Brazil with São Paulo State highlighted (upper left), São Paulo State with São Paulo city highlighted (lower left), and a municipal green-area coverage index choropleth highlighting Ecológico Chico Mendes and Lajeado-Izaura Pereira de Souza Franzolin urban parks (right).
